definitions.gloss: visiting a grave; paying respects at a grave
definitions.explanation: The act of visiting a family grave to clean it, offer flowers, incense, and food, and pray for the deceased. An important cultural practice in Japan.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}にお{墓参|はかまい}りに{行|い}く。
examples.english: I visit the grave during Obon.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}のお{墓参|はかまい}りに{家族|かぞく}で{行|い}ってきた。
examples.english: We went as a family to visit grandmother's grave.

examples.japanese: {毎年|まいとし}{春|はる}と{秋|あき}のお{彼岸|ひがん}には、{実家|じっか}に{帰|かえ}ってお{墓参|はかまい}りをするようにしている。
examples.english: Every year during the spring and autumn equinox weeks, I make it a point to go back home and visit the graves.

notes:
CULTURE:
お{墓参|はかまい}り is an important Japanese custom. Families typically visit graves during お{盆|ぼん} (mid-August), お{彼岸|ひがん} (equinox weeks in March and September), and {命日|めいにち} (death anniversaries). The visit involves cleaning the gravestone, offering {線香|せんこう} (incense), {花|はな} (flowers), and sometimes food or drink, and praying.

FORMS:
The plain form {墓参|はかまい}り (without お) is also used but sounds less polite. {墓参|ぼさん} is a more formal reading used in written contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{墓参|はかまい}りに{行|い}く (to go visit a grave)
- お{墓参|はかまい}りをする (to visit a grave)
